title: Scale factors and {{term:similar}} shapes
summary: Enlarge a shape by a scale factor, spot similar shapes, find a scale factor, and draw a similar shape from one side.
guide: Two shapes are {{term:similar}} when one is an enlargement of the other: matching angles are equal and every side is multiplied by the same number. That number is the {{term:scale-factor}}.

The classic mistake at this age is adding instead of multiplying. Adding 2 to each side of a 3 × 1 rectangle gives 5 × 3, which is a different shape: no longer long and thin. To enlarge, multiply every side.
Turning or flipping a shape does not stop it being similar. A scale factor does not have to be a whole number: 1.5 is fine.

engine.instruction-draw: Tap the vertices, then the first one again.
engine.instruction-tap: Tap the shapes similar to the orange rectangle.

enlarge.title: Enlarge by 2
enlarge.prompt: Enlarge the orange rectangle by scale factor 2 and draw the enlargement. Predict the side lengths first.
enlarge.hint: Multiply each side by 2: the side of 3 becomes 6. What does the short side become?
enlarge.success: Well done! 3 × 2 = 6 and 1 × 2 = 2. The 6 by 2 rectangle is the same shape, twice as big.
enlarge.why: Why doesn't adding 2 to each side make a similar rectangle?
enlarge.model: Adding 2 gives a 5 by 3 rectangle. In the original the long side is 3 times the short side, but 5 is not 3 times 3, so the shape is fatter. Multiplying by 2 keeps that: 6 is still 3 times 2.

feedback.empty: Tap the grid to draw the enlargement.
feedback.open: Your shape is still open. Tap the first vertex to close it.
feedback.crossed: The sides cross. Tap the vertices in order round the shape.
feedback.too-many-sides: A rectangle has only 4 vertices. Press Clear and try again.
feedback.too-few-sides: A rectangle has 4 vertices. You need one more.
feedback.not-similar: That rectangle is not similar to the orange one. Did you add 2 to each side? To enlarge, multiply each side by 2.
feedback.wrong-factor: Right shape, wrong size. The side of 3 must become 6.

which-similar.title: Which are similar?
which-similar.prompt: Tap every rectangle that is similar to the orange 2 by 1 rectangle.
which-similar.hint: For each rectangle, how many times longer is the long side than the short side? In the orange one it is 2 times.
which-similar.success: Well done! The green (4 by 2) and purple (2 by 4) rectangles are similar to the orange one; the purple one is just standing up.
which-similar.why: The blue rectangle (3 by 2) is 1 square bigger each way than the orange one. Why isn't it similar?
which-similar.model: Because 1 was added to each side instead of multiplying. The side of 2 became 3 (1.5 times) but the side of 1 became 2 (2 times). The sides did not grow by the same factor, so the shape changed.

feedback.added: The blue rectangle is 3 by 2: 1 was added to each side. Its long side is not 2 times its short side, so it is not similar.
feedback.one-way: The red rectangle is 4 by 1: only one side was doubled. Both sides must be multiplied by the same number.
feedback.extra: One rectangle you tapped is not similar. Tap it again to remove it.
feedback.missed: There is another similar rectangle. It might be turned round.

scale-factor.title: Find the scale factor
scale-factor.prompt: These two triangles are similar. What is the scale factor from the small triangle to the big one? Choose a number.
scale-factor.hint: Compare matching sides: what do you multiply 2 by to get 6?
scale-factor.success: Well done! The scale factor is 3: 2 × 3 = 6 and 1 × 3 = 3.
scale-factor.why: Why isn't the answer 4? After all, 6 − 2 = 4.
scale-factor.model: 4 is the difference between two sides, not the factor. The other side only grew by 2 (3 − 1 = 2), so the differences don't match. But both sides were multiplied by 3: 6 ÷ 2 = 3 and 3 ÷ 1 = 3.

feedback.difference: That is a difference: you subtracted. The scale factor says how many times bigger each side is.
feedback.side: 6 is a side length of the big triangle. The scale factor says how many times bigger the small side got.
feedback.too-big: Too big. The side of 1 is 3 in the big triangle.
feedback.too-small: Too small. What do you multiply 2 by to get 6?

draw-similar.title: Draw a similar rectangle
draw-similar.prompt: Draw a rectangle similar to the orange 2 by 4 rectangle, with a short side of 3. Predict the long side first.
draw-similar.hint: In the orange rectangle, how many times longer is the long side than the short side? The new one must be the same.
draw-similar.success: Well done! A 3 by 6 rectangle. The scale factor is 1.5: 2 × 1.5 = 3 and 4 × 1.5 = 6.
draw-similar.why: How did you work out the long side?
draw-similar.model: In the orange rectangle the long side is 2 times the short side (4 = 2 × 2). So in the new one the long side is 2 times 3, which is 6. Or use the scale factor: 3 ÷ 2 = 1.5 and 4 × 1.5 = 6.

feedback.empty: Tap the grid to draw the rectangle.
feedback.open: Your shape is still open. Tap the first vertex to close it.
feedback.crossed: The sides cross. Tap the vertices in order round the shape.
feedback.too-many-sides: A rectangle has only 4 vertices. Press Clear and try again.
feedback.too-few-sides: A rectangle has 4 vertices. You need one more.
feedback.not-similar: That rectangle is not similar. Did you draw 3 by 5? The short side grew by 1, but the long side must grow by the same factor, not the same amount.
feedback.wrong-factor: It is similar, but its short side is not 3. Count the squares.
